entries.final_answer: One new file rule_acceptance.go with two pure functions: evaluateRuleAcceptance (live: current evidence, including vetoes) and validateRuleMergeFact (immutable: the fact's listed evidence only). Both receive the base policy, its digest, the proposal, the rule name, the changed paths and the pipeline definition digests from the caller and do no Git I/O. Callers load objects: automerge.go and serve_protected.go call the live function; store.go (validateMergeEvent) and quarantine.go (validateReplicationMergeAt, which also serves the hn serve actor-chain check) call the fact function. The existing acceptance merge fact checks stay unchanged and still run when rule is absent.

entries.final_answer: Event gains Rule string `json:"rule,omitempty"` after Evidence, so every existing payload re-encodes byte-identically. validateEventContent rejects a non-empty Rule on every kind other than proposal.merged and requires the rule-name grammar (validPipelineName) on proposal.merged. verifyEvent also walks the top-level keys of each non-resource payload. It rejects any key that equals "rule" under case folding unless the key is exactly "rule", appears once, sits on proposal.merged and holds a non-empty JSON string. That catches rule null, rule "" and case variants that Go's decoder would otherwise drop or fold. No new event kind and no protocol version change.

AutomergeReviewers is a []string kind whose UnmarshalJSON rejects null and decodes an array of strings into a non-nil slice. When a field is absent it keeps its zero value, which means acceptance maintainers or no rule reviewers. validateOptionalPolicy then applies FR-002 to FR-005, with messages that name the rule and the field. entries.final_answer: Execution lists, sorted and unique, the current approve review of each counting reviewer and, for each base-policy pipeline, the latest passing result of each trusted runner. A counting reviewer is in trustedReviewers, is in the rule's reviewers when that field is set, and is never the author under acceptance mode rule. A result counts when its request was signed by a maintainer or a listed requester and names the pipeline definition digest at the head. A verifier requires every listed item to qualify on those terms, with at most one approval per reviewer and at most one result per runner per pipeline. The approvals must reach proposals.requiredApprovals and each pipeline must reach its requiredResults. Any other item invalidates the fact, including decisions, change requests, failed results, approvals the rule does not count and results whose request is not authorized.
